Author: T. Vinod Kumar

 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar

O R D E R:

Heard learned counsel for petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Roads & Buildings appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent No.4, and perused the record.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is that they are the inam land holders; that 1st petitioner is having an extent of Ac.0-15 gts in survey No.208 & 209, 2nd petitioner is having an extent of Ac.0- 07 gts in survey Nos.210 & 217 situated at Alagadapa Village, Miryalaguda Mandal, and Ac.0-35 gts in survey No.16 & 17, totaling to an extent of Ac.1.17 gts, situated at Chillepally Village, Nereducharla Mandal, Suryapet District; and that the respondents acquired the aforesaid land for the purpose of formation of approaches to the High Level Bridge across Musi River between Miryalaguda-Huzurnagar road, without passing any award and without paying any compensation,
which action it is contended as arbitrary, illegal and contrary to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'Act 30 of 2013').
3. Counter affidavit on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 3 & 4, is filed separately.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
4. By the counter affidavit filed on behalf of respondent No.3, sworn to on 11.11.2024, while denying that there is delay on part of the said respondent in settling the claims of petitioners, it is stated that the respondents are pursuing the matter by addressing letters to other respondents; that the Executive Engineer (R&B) Division had addressed a letter, dt.11.11.2024, to the Collector & District Magistrate of Nalgonda and Suryapet for taking necessary action for acquisition of the subject lands of the petitioners; that on 12.11.2024, the Executive Engineer had addressed letter to the Superintendent Engineer(R&B) Regional Office, Nalgonda, stating that land acquisition proposals were submitted duly mentioning the details of survey numbers as per survey report of the revenue authorities; that as the required ROW for construction of High Level Bridge from km 6/6 to 7/2 is not available, acquisition is to be made for additional ROW; and that approval of Form-A from the Government as per Section 10A & Rule 4 (i.e., exemption from Chapter-II & Chapter -III of the Act),
is required and accordingly requested to obtain approval of Form-A from the Government.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 to 3 thus submits that the authorities are already seized of the matter.

6. The 4th respondent, by the counter affidavit filed and sworn to on 09.12.2024, while admitting to the fact of petitioners' lands to an extent of Ac.0-36 gts and 96 sq. yards in survey Nos.208, 209,
210, 213, 214 and 215 situated at Alagadapa Village, Miryalaguda Mandal, being covered in the alignment of construction of high level bridge on Musi River on the road leading from Miryalaguda to Huzurnagar, had stated that the Executive Engineer, R&B Nalgonda has filed requisition for acquisition before the 4th respondent and on scrutiny, the acquisition authority had noted certain defects and accordingly, requested the requisitioning authority to file revised requisition along with Form-A exemption orders from the Government; and that on receipt of the revised requisition and exemption Form-A, necessary action for acquisition will be initiated and compensation would be paid.
7. I have taken note of the respective submissions made.
8.

The respondents, by their separate counter affidavits filed, do not dispute the fact of the lands of the petitioners being affected by the formation of approaches to the High Level Bridge across Musi River between Miryalaguda-Huzurnagar road, for which the authorities are required to acquire the lands of the petitioners.

9. Though the 3rd respondent, by the counter affidavit filed had claimed the authorities having initiated correspondence with other departments for acquiring the lands, the fact of the said respondent sending a request to the Collector & District Magistrate, Nalgonda, for acquiring the lands on 11.11.2024 i.e., on the same day as that of filing counter affidavit into this Court, only goes to show that the said respondent did not initiate action earlier even though the writ petition is filed in the month of December, 2023, and only to save himself from this Court examining the matter in detail, has claimed of the authorities having initiated proceedings for acquiring the lands of the petitioners.

10. Further, the 4th respondent having informed the Executive Engineer of the necessity to obtain exemption from conduct of Socio Economic Survey, for the said authority to initiate land acquisition proceedings, would also go to show that the respondent-authorities No.1 to 3 only as a mere eyewash have made the said statement of the said authority having initiated proceedings for acquiring the lands of the petitioners.

11. Even, now the requisition sent by the respondent No.1 to 3 on 11.11.2024 being an incomplete requisition, without obtaining necessary exemption from government for conduct of Socio Economic Survey, would further go to show that the said requisition is a defective requisition, which cannot be acted upon by the 4th respondent by initiating proceedings for acquiring the lands of the petitioners.

12. 13. However, as the respondents-authorities now claim to have initiated land acquisition proceedings, though being defective, this Court is of the view that the respondents-authorities are to be directed to complete the entire process of acquiring the lands of the petitioners to an extent of extent of Ac.0-15 gts in survey No.208 & 209, 2nd petitioner is having an extent of Ac.0-07 gts in survey Nos.210 & 217 situated at Alagadapa Village, Miryalaguda Mandal, and Ac.0-35 gts in survey No.16 & 17, situated at Chillepally Village, Nereducharla Mandal, Suryapet District, under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and complete the entire exercise, including payment of compensation to the petitioners, within a period of six (06) months from today.
14.
